newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds could rest case Wed. at Fla trial.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds could rest case Wed. at Fla trial.

text.p: Lawyers for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co said Tuesday they expected to rest their case Wednesday at the trial of a wrongful death lawsuit filed by the family of smoker Jean Connor, who died of lung cancer.

At a scheduling conference following Tuesday's testimony, Judge Bernard Nachman said rebuttal witnesses could be called Thursday, followed by a conference of lawyers to decide on the instructions to be given to the jury.
Closing arguments could then be given Friday morning with jury deliberations following. Each side was to be given two hours for closing statements, Nachman said.
The schedule was tentative, depending on the length of testimony of the final Reynolds' witness, rebuttal and legal arguments to follow.

Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, was sued by Dana Raulerson on behalf of the estate and children of her sister, Connor, who died in October 1995 at age 49. Connor began smoking as a teen-ager and eventually developed a three-pack-a-day habit.
Dominic Ciraulo, a Boston University psychiatrist and a specialist on addiction, was expected to be called to the witness stand Wednesday.
